terminal.emulator: direct PTY with raw byte writes

reference.capture: direct PTY byte stream with a synthetic xclip provider and ANSI-stripped stable text markers

normalization: Temporary checkout, synthetic HERMES_HOME, HOME, and xclip paths are represented by placeholders.
ANSI control sequences, cursor placement, colors, timestamps, session IDs, prompt faces, and dynamic working-directory text are not part of this contract.
The PTY window is explicitly set to 120 columns by 40 rows before process launch.
Ctrl+V is sent as the raw byte 0x16; no host clipboard is read or modified.
Linux provider selection is isolated by omitting Wayland and WSL variables and placing only the synthetic xclip provider first in PATH.
The fixture records the successful text path and preserves the empty-provider control as environment-sensitive where the image gateway was unavailable.

steps.precondition: Fresh synthetic HERMES_HOME and a synthetic xclip command returning clip-one plus two trailing newlines.
Fresh synthetic HERMES_HOME and a synthetic xclip command returning empty stdout.

output.image_fallback: environment-sensitive; no gateway response in the isolated direct-PTY run

environment_sensitive.reason: The TUI asks its gateway for clipboard image attachment after text providers return unusable data; the isolated direct PTY had no gateway response. OBS-0010 separately captured the no-provider miss message.

unknowns: Whether OSC52 text responses take precedence over native providers in remote, tmux, or SSH environments.
Image-only clipboard attachment, path paste, gateway image metadata, and attachment token rendering.
Provider behavior when xclip exits nonzero, returns binary-looking text, or exceeds the clipboard size cap.
